subject: maths
title: Long Multiplication
seo_title: Year 6 Long Multiplication Worksheets: 4-Digit by 2-Digit (KS2 SATs)
standard_code: Year 6: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
standard_text: Multiply multi-digit numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit whole number using the formal written method of long multiplication.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on long multiplication: 2-digit, 3-digit and 4-digit numbers × 2-digit numbers, the place-holder zero, finding mistakes and missing digits, and SATs-style word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Make one row for each digit: multiply by the ones, then by the tens. Then add the rows.
key_sub: Row 2 starts with a place-holder zero because it multiplies by tens: 47 × 36 = 282 + 1,410 = 1,692. Estimate first to check your answer.
body_html:
One row for each digit

Long multiplication is the formal written method for multiplying by a 2-digit number. You multiply the top number by one digit at a time, so you get two rows. Then you add the rows.

Row 1 multiplies by the ones digit. Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it starts with a place-holder zero (green) in the ones column. Write the exchanged digits small, and add them after you multiply.

4-digit × 2-digit, as in the SATs

A zero inside the number

405 × 32 = ?

Row 1: 5 × 2 = 10, write 0, exchange 1. 0 × 2 + 1 = 1. 4 × 2 = 8. So 405 × 2 = 810. Row 2: write 0, then 405 × 3 = 1,215, so 12,150. Add: 810 + 12,150 = 12,960.

Answer: 12,960

Estimate to check

Round each number and multiply in your head. 2,345 × 28 is about 2,000 × 30 = 60,000, so 65,660 makes sense. An answer like 23,450 is far too small.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
No place-holder zero (47 × 36 = 282 + 141 = 423)Row 2 is × 30, so write 0 first: 1,410
Forgetting an exchanged digit (47 × 6 = 242)Write it small and add it: 4 × 6 + 4 = 28, so 282
Adding the exchanged digit firstMultiply first, then add: 4 × 6 + 4 = 28, not (4 + 4) × 6
Multiplying by only one digit (47 × 36 = 282)Make a row for the ones and a row for the tens
Adding the rows wronglyUse column addition and add every exchanged digit

faq.q: How do you do long multiplication in Year 6?
faq.a: Multiply the top number by the ones digit to make row 1. Write a place-holder zero, then multiply by the tens digit to make row 2. Add the two rows with column addition, for example 47 × 36 = 282 + 1,410 = 1,692.

faq.q: Why do you put a zero in long multiplication?
faq.a: In 47 × 36 the 3 means 3 tens, so row 2 is 47 × 30, not 47 × 3. The place-holder zero in the ones column makes the row 1,410 instead of 141.

faq.q: What is the difference between short and long multiplication?
faq.a: Short multiplication is for multiplying by a one-digit number and gives one row. Long multiplication is for a two-digit number: you make one row for each digit and then add the rows.

faq.q: Is long multiplication in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Paper 1 (arithmetic) usually has long multiplication questions such as 4-digit × 2-digit. They are worth 2 marks, and a pupil can still get 1 mark for using the formal method with no more than one arithmetic error.

sets.title: Find the mistake and missing digits

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Row 1 is 7,618 × 4. The ? comes from 1 × 4 = 4, plus the exchanged 3 = 7. Write 7. Full row: 8 × 4 = 32, write 2, exchange 3; 1 × 4 + 3 = 7, write 7; 6 × 4 = 24, write 4, exchange 2; 7 × 4 + 2 = 30, write 30. Row 1 is 30,472.

items.q: Isla got 497 × 97 = 47,569. What mistake did she make?
c: Did not add an exchanged digit
items.e: Row 1 should be 3,479, not 2,839: 7 × 7 = 49, write 9, exchange 4; 9 × 7 + 4 = 67, write 7, exchange 6; 4 × 7 + 6 = 34, write 34. The exchanged digits were not added. The correct answer is 48,209.

items.q: Oliver worked out 961 × 49. Where is his mistake?
items.e: In row 1 the exchanged digits were not added: 1 × 9 = 9, write 9; 6 × 9 = 54, write 4, exchange 5; 9 × 9 + 5 = 86, write 86. Row 1 should be 8,649, not 8,149. The correct answer is 47,089.

sets.title: Word problems and estimating to check

items.q: A concert hall sells 2,172 tickets at £52 each. How much money does it take?
The school kitchen serves 383 lunches each week. How many lunches does it serve in 38 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 38 weeks × 383 lunches, so multiply 383 × 38. Row 1: 383 × 8 = 3,064. Row 2: 383 × 30 = 11,490 (write the place-holder 0, then 383 × 3 = 1,149). Add: 3,064 + 11,490 = 14,554.

items.q: Oliver says 3,164 × 47 = 148,708. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 3,164 rounds to 3,000 and 47 rounds to 50. 3,000 × 50 = 150,000. 148,708 is close to 150,000, so the answer is sensible. (It is also exactly right.)

items.q: Noah says 4,127 × 63 = 12,381. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 4,127 rounds to 4,000 and 63 rounds to 60. 4,000 × 60 = 240,000. 12,381 is far from 240,000, so the answer cannot be right. The correct answer is 260,001; Noah only multiplied by the ones digit.

items.q: A lorry carries 25 crates. Each crate has a mass of 479 kg. What is the total mass of the crates?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 crates × 479 kg, so multiply 479 × 25. Row 1: 479 × 5 = 2,395. Row 2: 479 × 20 = 9,580 (write the place-holder 0, then 479 × 2 = 958). Add: 2,395 + 9,580 = 11,975.

items.q: A cinema screen has 25 rows of seats with 26 seats in each row. How many seats are there?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 rows × 26 seats, so multiply 26 × 25. Row 1: 26 × 5 = 130. Row 2: 26 × 20 = 520 (write the place-holder 0, then 26 × 2 = 52). Add: 130 + 520 = 650.

items.q: A family pays £851 a month for their flat. How much do they pay in 24 months?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 months × £851, so multiply 851 × 24. Row 1: 851 × 4 = 3,404. Row 2: 851 × 20 = 17,020 (write the place-holder 0, then 851 × 2 = 1,702). Add: 3,404 + 17,020 = 20,424.

items.q: A garden centre has 59 trays of plants. Each tray holds 47 plants. How many plants is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 59 trays × 47 plants, so multiply 47 × 59. Row 1: 47 × 9 = 423. Row 2: 47 × 50 = 2,350 (write the place-holder 0, then 47 × 5 = 235). Add: 423 + 2,350 = 2,773.

items.q: A bakery bakes 176 loaves of bread every day. How many loaves does it bake in 28 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 28 days × 176 loaves, so multiply 176 × 28. Row 1: 176 × 8 = 1,408. Row 2: 176 × 20 = 3,520 (write the place-holder 0, then 176 × 2 = 352). Add: 1,408 + 3,520 = 4,928.

items.q: A theatre has 1,397 seats. Every seat is sold for all 24 shows of the Christmas pantomime. How many tickets are sold?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 shows × 1,397 tickets, so multiply 1,397 × 24. Row 1: 1,397 × 4 = 5,588. Row 2: 1,397 × 20 = 27,940 (write the place-holder 0, then 1,397 × 2 = 2,794). Add: 5,588 + 27,940 = 33,528.

items.q: A farm packs 144 eggs in each crate. It sends 26 crates on Monday and 38 crates on Tuesday. How many eggs does it send altogether?
A school has £6,000 to spend. It buys 24 laptops at £235 each. How much money is left?
items.e: Step 1: the cost. Row 1: 235 × 4 = 940. Row 2: 235 × 20 = 4,700 (write the place-holder 0, then 235 × 2 = 470). Add: 940 + 4,700 = 5,640. So the laptops cost £5,640. Step 2: £6,000 − £5,640 = £360 left.

items.q: A factory makes 2,272 toy cars each day. How many toy cars does it make in 23 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 days × 2,272 toy cars, so multiply 2,272 × 23. Row 1: 2,272 × 3 = 6,816. Row 2: 2,272 × 20 = 45,440 (write the place-holder 0, then 2,272 × 2 = 4,544). Add: 6,816 + 45,440 = 52,256.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 26 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 26 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 26. Row 1: 144 × 6 = 864. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2,880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 864 + 2,880 = 3,744.

items.q: Harry says 689 × 52 = 35,828. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 689 rounds to 700 and 52 rounds to 50. 700 × 50 = 35,000. 35,828 is close to 35,000, so the answer is sensible. (It is also exactly right.)

items.q: A ticket for a theme park costs £125. A school buys 36 tickets for a Year 6 trip. How much does it pay?
items.e: Equal groups: 36 tickets × £125, so multiply 125 × 36. Row 1: 125 × 6 = 750. Row 2: 125 × 30 = 3,750 (write the place-holder 0, then 125 × 3 = 375). Add: 750 + 3,750 = 4,500.

items.q: A delivery driver drives 1,619 km each week. How far does she drive in 23 weeks?
Amelia says 2,345 × 28 = 23,450. Estimate to check. Is her answer sensible?
items.e: 2,345 rounds to 2,000 and 28 rounds to 30. 2,000 × 30 = 60,000. 23,450 is far from 60,000, so the answer cannot be right. The correct answer is 65,660; Amelia forgot the place-holder 0 in the second row.

items.q: A coach has 53 seats. It is full on every one of its 24 trips to the seaside this summer. How many passengers is that altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 trips × 53 passengers, so multiply 53 × 24. Row 1: 53 × 4 = 212. Row 2: 53 × 20 = 1,060 (write the place-holder 0, then 53 × 2 = 106). Add: 212 + 1,060 = 1,272.

items.q: Ava swims 64 lengths of a 25 m pool over a term. How far does she swim?
items.e: Equal groups: 64 lengths × 25 m, so multiply 64 × 25. Row 1: 64 × 5 = 320. Row 2: 64 × 20 = 1,280 (write the place-holder 0, then 64 × 2 = 128). Add: 320 + 1,280 = 1,600.
